decisions.rationale: The full disease name in the title refers to one specific disease, aspartylglucosaminuria, with no further categorization.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (title is annotated)

decisions.rationale: Repeated mention of the same specific disease in the abstract. Duplicate mentions are each annotated.
Abbreviation of aspartylglucosaminuria. The short form is a separate mention from the long form.
Lysosomal storage disorder denotes a family of multiple distinct specific diseases rather than one definable disease.
Deficiency is a very general term describing a biochemical state and is explicitly excluded.
Mental retardation is a grey-area umbrella term covering many etiologically distinct conditions, so it corresponds to a family of diseases rather than one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: Examples 11 (grey-area terms annotated as Disease Class)

decisions.rationale: The word disease on its own is a very general term and is excluded.
AGU is used as a modifier of the noun phrase Finnish AGU patients, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
Seborrhoeic describes the appearance of the skin rather than naming a disease and is not linked to a specific disease definition.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (disease definition not met); What NOT to Annotate 4 (descriptive/general terms)

decisions.rationale: Facial angiofibroma is a specific tumour type with one definition and no further categorization.
Tumours is a generic term used appositively for a family of tumour types here. Tumour terms are retained, but the mention refers to a class rather than one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class); What NOT to Annotate 4 (tumor/cancer terms retained)

decisions.rationale: Tuberous sclerosis is a single named genetic disease with a specific definition.
Leucoedema is a named oral mucosal condition with its own specific definition.
Gingival overgrowths is a descriptive finding term similar to abnormalities and is not a named specific disease or disease class.
AGU modifies the noun phrase buccal mucosa and patients in the comparison, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
The phrase refers to two separate disease mentions, fibroepithelial hyperplasias and epithelial hyperplasias, joined by or, so it is one contiguous Composite Mention.
AGU modifies the noun phrase patients mucosal lesions, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
